ev.q: CDC analyzed serologic test results from persons aged 14--49 years who participated in NHANES 2005--2008.
HSV-2 seroprevalence was greater among women (20.9%) than men (11.5%) (p<0.001).

Overall HSV-2 seroprevalence from NHANES 2005--2008 was 16.2%

By race/ethnicity, HSV-2 seroprevalence was approximately three times greater among non-Hispanic blacks (39.2%) as among non-Hispanic whites (12.3%) (p<0.001).

methods_quotes.q: Differences in seroprevalence among categories of participants (e.g., sex or age group) were assessed using the Wald chi-square test.
Statistical software was used to generate seroprevalence estimates and 95% confidence intervals.
All seroprevalence estimates were weighted using medical examination weights of the survey
accounting for survey participants' unequal probabilities of selection and adjustments for nonresponse.
